commands.name: flow
commands.description: Show the flow in a pane: managers, their workers, the reviewer and handed-over PRs. /flow inbox lists the open questions and the decisions agents made (/flow inbox decisions lists them all, /flow inbox <id> shows one in full), /flow ok keeps every open decision (/flow ok <id|owner|topic> takes those, or the default of a question), /flow no <id> [what instead] undoes a decision, /flow answer <id> <choice> answers any question addressed to main, /flow status shows what the agents cost (estimates at API list prices), /flow checks lists the after-deploy checks that need a person (pass or fail them), /flow preflight shows the current pre-flight round, /flow close closes it, /flow lite <task> runs one task as just a manager and its workers (no pre-flight, no reviewer agent) to save tokens, /flow resume picks up unfinished flow work, /flow approve <pr> lets the reviewer merge a PR that awaits your approval, /flow reject <pr> [reason] (alias /flow drop) turns down a handover that awaits approval or is pending, /flow push starts the push of the batch the reviewer checked and saved (push_mode confirm; /flow push back <pr> sends one PR back, /flow push drop returns them all), /flow hold <target> [batch|released] keeps a deploy target from deploying and /flow release <target> lets it, /flow clean lists leftover worktrees and branches (--yes removes them)

commands.name: flow-tasks
commands.description: Pick tasks from a task source (.claude/flow/sources/<name>.md) and start a manager for each

tools.name: handover
tools.description: Hand an approved PR to the flow reviewer (managers, after reviewing a worker's PR; leave the branch alone afterwards). Refused unless the PR description has a ## Verification section (Ran, Exercised, Not verified); the refusal shows the format.

tools.name: release
tools.description: Release at merge (release setting on); the reviewer calls it once per batch after the full check, before the push. "cut": moves the changelog's ## [Unreleased] lines into a new version section, bumps the version (patch, or the highest of the PRs' release field and flow:minor / flow:major labels), returns the commit command; does not commit or push; a repeat for the same PRs is refused. "publish" (release_github on, after the release commit is pushed): tags v<version>, pushes the tag, creates the GitHub Release; failures come back as "Not published".

tools.name: ask
tools.description: Ask structured questions (a batch) instead of prose. A worker's go to its manager, a manager's to main; main cannot ask. Give options and a recommended default. Non-blocking: go on with the default and say so in your report; you get a message if the answer differs. Blocking: end your turn and wait; you are woken with the answer. A recurring kind of question gets a stable kebab-case topic.

tools.name: fyi
tools.description: Record a reversible choice you took yourself (a threshold, wording, a name, a default, styling) as a non-blocking decision (ids d1, d2, ...) the user can keep or undo. A worker's go to its manager, a manager's to main. Never stop for it; you get a message only if it is undone. Irreversible or product-defining choices (what customers pay for, who receives data, deleting data) are asks. Main cannot call it.

tools.name: preflight
tools.description: Managers only. File your pre-flight after looking over your task (no workers yet). Worker starts are refused until you have, and until blocking questions are answered.

tools.name: answer
tools.description: Answer questions addressed to you in the decision inbox. Decisions (mcp__flow__fyi) work the same way: choice Keep, or defaults: true, keeps them; any other choice or free text undoes the decision and messages the owner. Main may answer any decision. choice: an option's letter, number or text, or free text. defaults: true takes the default of your open decisions and non-blocking questions; a blocking question needs an explicit answer or its id in ids.

tools.name: standing
tools.description: Main only. Standing answers: rules that answer a recurring decision-inbox question at once. "list": rules and suggestions (questions answered the same way 3+ times); with no rules it offers starting rules, accepted with "add" and seed/seeds. "add": topic or match (case-insensitive regex on the question), answer, optional blocking (default false: blocking questions are left to you) and from. "remove": id (rules without one: file and position, e.g. personal:1). "dismiss": id of a suggestion (or "all"): it is not offered again. kinds ["fyi"] makes a rule that keeps matching recorded decisions (answer "Keep"); without kinds a rule answers ordinary questions only. Topics compare ignoring case, _ - and spaces, and one trailing s. escalate: true makes matching questions blocking and yours alone; answer "default" takes the question's own default (non-blocking only).

tools.name: check
tools.description: Main only (the reviewer may close checks that carry a verify command). After-deploy checks that need a person. "list": open checks and follow-ups. "pass": id or ids. "fail": id and note; creates a follow-up. "skip": id or ids and note (check no longer applies). "started": id of a failed check and manager.

tools.name: note
tools.description: A manager's notes on disk, kept across restarts. With text, appends a dated line (kind "decision" for what the user decided, else "progress"); without text, returns the notes.

tools.name: reviewer
tools.description: The reviewer's worklist; only the reviewer calls it. "list": pending and taken handovers. "take" (pr), "done" (pr, sha, report) or "back" (pr, reason). "done" also deletes the merged PR branch on the remote and appends "| flaky: <test>" for tests that failed then passed under test_slot. With push_mode confirm, "ready" (prs, sha, base_sha, check, version?) saves the checked batch for the user's /flow push instead of pushing.

tools.name: queue
tools.description: (Old name of reviewer; use reviewer.) The reviewer's worklist; only the reviewer calls it. "list": pending and taken handovers. "take" (pr), "done" (pr, sha, report) or "back" (pr, reason). "done" also deletes the merged PR branch on the remote and appends "| flaky: <test>" for tests that failed then passed under test_slot. With push_mode confirm, "ready" (prs, sha, base_sha, check, version?) saves the checked batch for the user's /flow push instead of pushing.

tools.name: push
tools.description: Main only, on the user's word: release the batch the reviewer saved because push_mode is confirm; others are refused. "list": the ready batch. "push": release it. "send-back" (pr): return one PR; the rest is rebuilt and re-checked. "drop": discard the batch and return every PR.

tools.name: status
tools.description: The flow at a glance: managers, workers and reviewer with status and last report, and handed-over PRs, scoped to your own subtree (main and the reviewer see everything). Newest 5 finished PRs only; with pr, that PR in full.

tools.name: deploy
tools.description: Per-target deploy gates. The reviewer calls "gate" (target, sha) before each target and gets exactly one of "Go", "Held: <why>" or "Awaits approval: <qid>"; on the last two skip that target for this batch. Only the user's "deploy" answer lets a confirm target through. Call "deployed" (target, sha, ok) after each target. Main only, on the user's word: "hold" (target, until, reason?) and "release" (target). "list": every target with mode, hold, last deployed sha, approval and pending env changes. Env changes of a handed-over PR come first in the gate: "Awaits env: <qids>" (skip the target), "Held: env change NAME declined" (skip until main releases it), or "Go, first apply env:" with one exact command per change: run each (non-zero exit fails the target), call "env-applied" (target, names), then deploy.

tools.name: clean
tools.description: Leftover worktrees flow made (under .claude/worktrees/, on flow/ branches, or recorded for a terminal session, wherever they live) and local branches of finished work. The person's own worktrees are never touched. Dry run unless apply is true; apply removes only clean work that is on the base or in a merged PR (or pushed with its PR closed); uncommitted, unpushed, locked and live work is never touched.

tools.name: migrations
tools.description: Read-only. Reports migration-number clashes and the next free number for the migrations_dir setting: per PR each added migration as ok, clash or at-or-below (not above the base's highest). For each non-ok one: the next free number, the git mv to run, and where the PR's files mention the old number.

tools.name: plan
tools.description: Declare which packages (for main, tasks) wait for others; the plugin refuses early starts and tells you when they are ready. "add": nodes [{id, title, after?, until?}]: id is the agent name you will start (or its prefix before -N), after lists node ids, until is "merged" (default) or "reported". "list" (main may pass owner), "done" (id, note?), "block" (id, reason), "remove" (id; only a waiting or ready node nothing depends on).

tools.name: test_slot
tools.description: A lock on heavy test runs: only test_slots of them run at once across all worktrees. "acquire" before a whole suite or any run over about a minute; if it says queued, wait as the answer tells you (grant file or message), then call acquire once to confirm. "release" when the run ends or fails, with result "pass"/"fail" and on fail failed_tests (exact names; a pass after a fail with the same label on the same sha is reported as flaky; a pass on another tree is a fix). "status": holders and waiters.

tools.name: guard_tests
tools.description: The repo-wide tests the guard_tests setting requires for your diff. Call it before gh pr create, normally with no arguments. Run each listed test under mcp__flow__test_slot and list each under `Ran:` in the PR's ## Verification section; handover refuses otherwise.

tools.name: session
tools.description: Workers outside this session: another harness (codex, gemini, opencode, claude, or your own command line) in a terminal (Orca or tmux, per the mode setting) the user can watch. "start" (name, brief, harness?, command?) makes a worktree on flow/<name> and starts the harness with the worker rules and the brief; its report comes back as a "flow session:" message. "send" (name, text), "keys" (name, keys), "read" (name, lines?), "restart" (name), "list", "stop" (name, remove_worktree?).

tools.name: settings
tools.description: Main only. flow settings, for /flow init. action "show": what init detected (base branch, remote, gh, test and check command candidates from the repo) and the Core settings in each layer (/config, the repo file, the personal file). action "write": layer "repo" (.claude/flow.json, committed, shared) or "personal" (uncommitted), values {key: value}; merges into the file, null removes a key. Plain settings only (strings, numbers, booleans, lists); keys and secrets are refused, they never go in settings. A file that is not valid JSON is never overwritten.

tools.name: demo
tools.description: Main only. The /flow init demo. action "start": the free replay in the Flow pane (canned agents, no model calls, nothing written); "stop" ends it. "cleanup": after a real demo, removes its worktree and branch (only flow/flow-demo* names; refused while a demo agent is running). "status": whether the replay runs and which demo agents exist.

tools.name: decide_eval
tools.description: Main only. Replays flow's history (inbox decisions, test failures, merge conflicts, handoffs, and model sizing at spawn, and whether a task needs a manager) through the decision API; reports agreement, fall-through, confidence and estimated savings per question. Uses the configured decision_api and its /config key; writes ids, labels and confidences (no texts, no key) to decide-eval.json in the flow state dir. Refused when decision_api is off, unless dry_run (sizes and samples, no network).

tools.name: size_ab_report
tools.description: Main only. Reads the cost ledger and log of the size_ab A/B (Jev sizing on even local days, the Size line alone on odd days) and prints, per arm and role, packages, $ per merged PR, how many needed a -N successor and the model mix; says when an arm has too few packages to conclude. Read-only, no network.

tools.name: arms
tools.description: Best-of-N (setting best_of_n): the manager that started competing arms (<pkg>-a, <pkg>-b, <pkg>-c, each with an "Arm: <letter> of <N>" line in its brief) picks the winner. "pick" (group = the package name without the arm letter, pr = the winner's PR, reason): closes the other arms' open PRs with a comment (their branches stay), logs the pick, and returns each arm's cost so far and which losing arms still run (stop those with TaskStop yourself). Only the picked arm's PR can then be handed over. A repeat with the same PR is a no-op; another PR is refused. "report": per group each arm's outcome (won, lost, pending), merged or not, $ per arm and the overhead of the group over the winner; a manager sees its own groups, main all.
